The Cover
The image President Trump posted to Truth Social on Monday: a doctored version of the AP’s 2024 Butler rally photo, with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in his place. Meme: @GrandOldMemes; original photo: Evan Vucci, AP.
The News

The National Wire

The Lead

Nvidia Takes Its Boss Back, and Trump Posts a Meme

Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive on Monday, less than two weeks after he was forced to resign over revelations of extramarital affairs, one of them with a suspected Chinese spy, the BBC reports. The chipmaker's board had at first turned down his offer to return; President Trump says he "made the deal" to get Huang his job back, and both the president and the company are facing criticism from lawmakers.

Hours later, Trump posted the image on today's cover to Truth Social with no caption: a doctored version of the Associated Press photo of him after the 2024 shooting at his rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, with Huang in his place, holding up a red bra, GV Wire reports. In a CNBC interview Trump suggested the scandal could help Huang, saying, "Sex sells, fellas," and in a separate post called him "a Great Patriot and National Treasure."

Investors cheered the return. Nvidia's shares jumped 31 percent on Monday, adding almost $1 trillion to its value, the BBC reports.

1

Update: The Iowa Blast Is Back On for Wednesday

A federal appeals court on Monday declined to block the Army from detonating five tons of unstable explosives at a munitions plant in Iowa, and the Army says it will go ahead Wednesday morning, CBS reports. Environmental groups had warned the blast could send a plume of toxic lead into the surrounding area; the government says the material has become unstable and could explode on its own.

The Market

S&P 500, daily close through Monday, Nov. 23. Data: Yahoo Finance.

Stocks came roaring back Monday: the S&P 500 rose 4.7 percent and the Nasdaq gained 6.5 percent, CBS reports. Friday's sell-off had pushed the S&P into a correction, a drop of 10 percent or more from its high; Monday's close leaves it about 7 percent below its October 6 peak, out of correction territory for now.

The Home Wire

2

Niagara Falls · Budget Night at City Hall

The Niagara Falls City Council meets today to consider amendments to Mayor Robert Restaino's proposed 2027 budget, the Niagara Gazette reports. The plan totals $107.6 million, $4.1 million more than this year's, with a separate $34.5 million capital budget.

3

Buffalo · Tops Lawsuit Against Social Media Dismissed

New York's highest court, the Court of Appeals, rejected a lawsuit filed on behalf of victims and families of the 2022 Tops supermarket shooting that argued social media companies helped radicalize the gunman, WIVB reports. The ruling found the platforms are not liable, WGRZ reports.

4

Webster · The Town vs. the Reindeer

The town of Webster has ordered Dennis McCormick to move the 20-foot inflatable reindeer outside his home on Holt Road, Rochester First reports. He says it's never been an issue, and he's weighing his options.

The Marquee

5

Adam Driver Joins the X-Men, as the Villain

Adam Driver, Kylo Ren in the last "Star Wars" trilogy, told Seth Meyers about playing Mister Sinister, a shape-shifting, mind-reading scientist, the main villain in Marvel's upcoming "X-Men" film, Variety reports.

6

Hila Klein Leaves the "H3 Podcast"

Hila Klein is leaving the "H3 Podcast," a month after it came out that her husband and co-host, Ethan Klein, had a six-month affair, Variety reports. "I'm devastated that things have come to this," she said in a post on the show's Instagram.

7

Tonight on TV

"Dancing With the Stars" hands out the Mirrorball trophy in its finale tonight, and a new Miss Universe is crowned, TVLine reports.

The Gridiron

Bills: The One Seed Is in Reach

With the Jaguars and Bengals both losing this week, the Bills can lock up the AFC's top seed, which has eluded them throughout Josh Allen's career, by winning the rest of their conference games, Buffalo Rumblings reports. The Bengals fell 22–20 to the Commanders on a last-second field goal Monday night, ProFootballTalk reports. Before Thursday's game, the team will honor restaurateur Russell Salvatore, a longtime supporter, WGRZ reports.

Jets: A Win, and an Argument

Sunday's win in Los Angeles was the Jets' first in five weeks, and Gang Green Nation reports the fan base is split between enjoying it and worrying about draft position. Next: at Miami on Sunday.

The Sunday Tax · Week 12

Josh won Week 11 with 11 right and takes the $85 pot. Week 12 is open: picks at tally.so/r/RGOakJ, standings at benthambulletin.github.io/pool. $5 a week, straight-up winners, the pot to the best record, and anyone with the link can play. Sheets lock at each kickoff; first game Wednesday at 8, Packers at Rams.

Sun's out, warmth isn't. Upper 30s, barely a breeze, and 24 tonight. Bring the hoses in or buy new ones in April.

Turkey Trot Watch · Thursday 6 a.m. to noon

Day two, and the forecast is holding. For North Tonawanda, the weather service still has the rain waiting until after 1 p.m. Thursday, now with a 70 percent chance once it comes, under cloudy skies with a high near 43. Wednesday night bottoms out around 29, and the east wind picks up Thursday, 7 to 15 mph with gusts as high as 30. Translation for the six of you: it's dry for the race and cold at the start, so dress for the 30s and the wind, not the high. And Thursday night is a soaker, so whoever's driving home from Derek's, take it easy.

On This Day

November 24, 1971 — A man who bought his ticket as "Dan Cooper" hijacked Northwest Orient Flight 305 between Portland and Seattle, traded the passengers for $200,000 in twenty-dollar bills and four parachutes, and jumped from the back of the plane into the dark somewhere between Seattle and Reno. The "D.B." was a mistake by the press that stuck. In 1980 a boy found $5,800 of the ransom, rotting in a package, with serial numbers that matched. The FBI weighed more than 800 suspects, never named him, and moved its resources to other cases in 2016.
